specification.problem: Characterize which decompositions of a two-outcome generalized quantum measurement into a continuous stochastic feedback process are possible when each iteration is a weak measurement from interaction with a qubit probe under a constant interaction Hamiltonian, with arbitrary unitary pulses allowed between iterations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction of a qubit-system, qubit-probe weak-measurement feedback loop. Only the abstract's qualitative result is used: achievable generalized measurements have two distinct singular values. The specific Hamiltonian, probe state, and pulse protocol are not given.

symbols.meaning: Kraus operators of a two-outcome generalized measurement
symbols.domain: Linear operators on the system Hilbert space
Hermitian operator on system tensor probe

equations.label: Two-outcome completeness
equations.description: Completeness relation for a two-outcome generalized measurement.
equations.justification: Standard definition of a generalized measurement; the abstract mentions two-outcome measurements.

equations.label: Weak measurement step
equations.description: One weak-measurement iteration from a short interaction with a qubit probe, followed by probe readout.
equations.justification: An assumed standard model of probe-induced weak measurement; the abstract does not give the exact form.

registers.name: P
registers.role: Probe qubit, freshly prepared each iteration and read out

specification.initial_state: System in an arbitrary state rho; probe in assumed fixed state |phi> each iteration.

steps.description: Prepare a fresh probe qubit in |phi>.
Apply the constant interaction e^{-iH_int dt} for short time dt between system and probe.
Measure the probe in a fixed basis, giving outcome k and applying the Kraus operator M_k to the system.
Apply an arbitrary system unitary pulse chosen by feedback from the record so far; repeat until the accumulated product of Kraus operators realizes the target two-outcome measurement.

specification.measurement: Each iteration measures the probe qubit in a fixed (assumed computational) basis, giving a binary outcome k that updates the system via M_k. The overall two-outcome result is inferred from the accumulated outcome record.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Record the probe outcomes and use them to choose feedback unitary pulses and decide when to stop. Map the final record to the overall binary outcome of the target generalized measurement. The abstract does not give the explicit rule.
assumptions: Standard Kraus model of a probe-induced weak measurement
Fresh probe per iteration with feedback pulses depending on prior outcomes
Probe readout in a fixed computational basis
missing_information: Probe initial state and readout basis
Stopping criterion for the continuous decomposition
Explicit rule mapping the outcome record to the final binary outcome
